rulings.ruling: cairn is a self-hosted personal assistant for people who write code: code work and personal affairs in one loop, one person and not a team.
Every trade-off first asks whether a second person can run it, then whether it differentiates; replaces self-use first.
The semantic axis is the machine-verified, evidence-bound merge gate (ADR 0026 / 0028); a verdict counts only for the patch digest it judged.
The runtime axis follows the Multica runtime model: runtime = one computer x one CLI tool, daemon as runtime, self-hosted single data root.

Approvals bind the irreversible-action boundary, not a mandatory lifecycle stage: merge/send/submit-class actions gate at the moment of effect via the action registry; the phase machine stays as the work-lifecycle spine for code output.
Chat apps are entry points, not the residence: Telegram, Slack (DM-only) and WeChat iLink are the IM entries; further platforms stay C class.
Electron desktop on all three OSes is decided; Windows and Linux join the shipped macOS app.
No team features: no shared channels, roles and permissions, or team billing; another person runs their own copy.

Today Cairn runs on the user's own machines, with no project-run hosted control plane and no resold compute. Direction: an official paid hosted service, Cairn Cloud, is in scope and not yet available (no free cloud tier; zero-markup BYOK first, optional model credits later), with its control plane, orchestration and billing in a separate private repository; local execution credentials stay on the user's own machines.

This repository stays Apache-2.0 open source with DCO sign-off and no CLA, and free self-hosting with full functionality stays un-gated (only the private rotating eval holdout stays unpublished). Nothing is sold today; the one paid offering in scope is the hosted service in positioning.hosted-cloud.
Remaining direction work is tracked on the owner's roadmap board as the single checklist entry; no in-repo plan tracker.
Evaluation and harness self-improvement stay in scope; judged adoption and self-evolution are not built (the in-repo bench and adoption judge were removed on 2026-11-16).
One chief; the entry is chosen by the user; output that is code passes the gates; whether a PR opens is only how the code lands.
The eval suite's task set, scorers and run configuration (eval/**) are protected paths; no change may edit what judges it.
Test layering and blast-radius rules live here; use real e2e for complex features, fixture surfaces for regression.
The canonical color and geometry token table lives here; UI code consumes tokens, not literals.
